opening_message:
Ticket 1: Keith Mclaughlin (employee ID E032) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E032.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Keith Mclaughlin (E032) is a full-time Analyst requesting write access to Source Code. Full-time employees qualify for up to write access; admin is only for the owning role (Engineer), so write is the maximum allowed. Requested level (write) equals the maximum, so recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Analyst (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security record for E032 shows contractor with basic security training, not full-time. Contractors max is read unless they have advanced training (never admin). Requested write exceeds maximum, so recommend granting read.
reason: There is conflicting evidence on employment type: HR reports E032 as full_time (max write for Source Code since Analyst doesn't own it), while Security reports contractor with basic training (max read, since write requires advanced training). Because the facts conflict and granting write would violate policy if the contractor record is accurate, read is the level that is valid under both interpretations and does not exceed any allowed maximum. Requested write exceeds the contractor maximum, so I grant read.
